done_when: each forge work round and each forge close appends one JSON line per step (worker round, review, CI wait) to .git/forge/timings.jsonl, never committed, with the item, the step, the model and effort where one ran, start time, seconds taken and outcome; a failed write never fails the command; a test through the real commands proves the lines

findings.body: The timing tests exercise successful Claude workers and unsuccessful Codex turns, but never assert a timing record after Claude fails. These use different failure paths: `src/forge/worker.py:303–304` raises a refusal for Claude, whereas the tested Codex failure returns a status. The existing failure test at `tests/test_worker.py:122–126` checks only command output. Losing the timing record or recording a successful outcome on Claude failure would therefore pass the suite. Add a real `forge work` failure scenario using `STUB_CLAUDE_EXIT`, and assert that it appends a failed worker-round record with the required timing and model fields.
findings.title: Not done: prove failed Claude worker timings through forge work

why: Forge records no timings, so nobody can tell how long worker rounds, reviews and CI waits take or which models and steps are worth tuning
